instruction:
On `node1`, add at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap, active at boot
and preferred over any disk-backed swap.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'node=%s ip=%s\n' "$NODE_NAME" "$NODE_IP"
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
uname -a
cat /etc/os-release
printf '%s\n' '--- memory ---'
free -m
printf '%s\n' '--- active swap ---'
cat /proc/swaps
printf '%s\n' '--- swap config ---'
grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' /etc/fstab | sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' || true
printf '%s\n' '--- zram capability ---'
command -v zramctl || true
modinfo zram 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,12p' || true
printf '%s\n' '--- relevant units ---'
systemctl list-unit-files 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'zram|swap' || true

commands.command:
set -eu
install -d -m 0755 /usr/local/sbin
cat > /usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-start <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
modprobe zram num_devices=1
if grep -q '^/dev/zram0[[:space:]]' /proc/swaps; then
    exit 0
fi
zramctl --reset /dev/zram0 2>/dev/null || true
zramctl --algorithm lzo --size 512M /dev/zram0
mkswap -L zram0 /dev/zram0
swapon --priority 100 /dev/zram0
ANTRIEB_EOF
cat > /usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-stop <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
if grep -q '^/dev/zram0[[:space:]]' /proc/swaps; then
    swapoff /dev/zram0
fi
zramctl --reset /dev/zram0 2>/dev/null || true
ANTRIEB_EOF
chmod 0755 /usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-start /usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-stop
cat > /etc/systemd/system/zram-swap.service <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Compressed in-memory swap on zram
Documentation=man:zramctl(8) man:swapon(8)

After=systemd-modules-load.service
Before=swap.target umount.target
Conflicts=umount.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-start
ExecStop=/usr/local/sbin/zram-swap-stop

[Install]
WantedBy=swap.target
ANTRIEB_EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable zram-swap.service
systemctl is-enabled zram-swap.service
systemctl cat zram-swap.service

agent_report.summary: Configured node1 with 512 MiB of lzo-compressed zram swap at priority 100. It is enabled at boot and remained healthy after the mandatory restart.
actions_performed: Installed a Xenial kernel package containing the required zram module because the original minimal kernel omitted it.
Activated /dev/zram0 as 536870912-byte compressed swap with priority 100.
Restarted node1 and verified persistence, system health, and a changed boot identity.

evidence.requirement: At least 512 MB compressed in-memory swap is active
evidence.summary: Shows /dev/zram0 active with a 536870912-byte capacity and lzo compression.
Shows zram-swap.service enabled and active before and after the persistence restart.

evidence.requirement: zram is preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: Shows live priority 100, the configured priority command, and no active non-zram swap.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID 5bcd056e-85d7-442c-8524-8a23a9ab66bb, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 12d32f1e-16bc-40bd-86b1-98a2c30b0240, and recovered system plus zram swap state.

requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap is active on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct observations before and after the persistence restart show /dev/zram0 active as swap, backed by a 536,870,912-byte zram device using the lzo compressor. The reported usable swap is 524,284 KiB, exceeding 512 decimal MB and reflecting only the normal swap-header reduction from the configured 512 MiB device.

requirements.requirement: The compressed swap is activated automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline showed the service enabled and active. A bounded restart was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unreachable, its boot ID changed, and the recovered system again showed the service enabled and active with /dev/zram0 mounted as swap.

requirements.requirement: The in-memory swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: The live zram swap has priority 100, the persistent startup command configures that priority, and both pre- and post-restart checks found no active non-zram swap.

evaluation.overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has persistent, lzo-compressed 512 MiB zram swap at priority 100, with no disk-backed swap active. The mandatory post-completion restart protocol is coherent: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement and disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered node and zram service. The fixed final boot identity agrees with the executor's post-restart observation.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not themselves inventory the zram service or installed packages in detail; those outcomes rely on direct executor commands. The global snapshot nevertheless independently confirms the final boot identity, kernel, package-manager consistency, and absence of failed services.
There was no application data or multi-node cluster state in this standalone task to validate beyond node health and the configured zram service.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the service and scripts, refreshing package metadata, installing the available kernel/module packages, selecting that kernel, and performing the two restarts all had clear causal roles in supplying the missing zram module, completing the task, or validating boot persistence. The briefly failed service start exposed the missing module and was corrected; the intermediate malformed legacy-GRUB default was immediately repaired. Final observations show no failed services, package inconsistency, new listening sockets, or abandoned temporary artifacts.
